overall_assessment: The bounded proposal is ready for explicit user validation. The [official primary documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-instagram-login/messaging-api.md) independently confirms a maximum of 1000 UTF-8 bytes for message text. Replacing the two quoted character limits therefore addresses a concrete provider incompatibility. It meaningfully reduces the permitted length of some non-ASCII outbound Instagram messages and requires renewed approval, while remaining within the existing text-reply capability and shared ownership boundaries. The proposal explicitly preserves WhatsApp behavior, ingress limits, existing consumers and later checkpoint obligations. Byte counting adds ordinary linear work; the shared route policy, authoritative server validation and existing single OutboundService are proportionate and structurally sound. Operational behavior is clear: reject before dispatch claim or provider HTTP, give actionable feedback and preserve valid text without truncation or splitting. Planned ASCII, accented-character and emoji boundaries, real backend/browser coverage and compatibility regressions adequately address this correction. This assessment covers the immutable proposal and its quoted governing clauses; implementation conformity and execution evidence were not reviewed.
recommended_path: Present the exact normative delta for explicit user validation. After approval, implement and prove the bounded server-and-browser correction in the admitted paths while retaining the specified WhatsApp, ingress, shared-owner and consumer contracts. This review grants no implementation or delivery acceptance.
